title: Responder orchestration and service degradation guidelines
author: Samira Patel
content:
Summary

This document defines a responder-centric orchestration pattern for incidents that cause partial service degradation or feature-level customer impact. It complements generic incident runbooks by focusing on choreography: how roles hand off, what system-level thresholds trigger automated mitigation, and standard status-page/customer communication templates tailored for degradations (not full outages).

Scope

- Applies to Redwood-hosted API endpoints, Dedicated pools, and customer-facing Console services.
- Focuses on incidents where availability is nominal but user-facing latency, error rates, or correctness regressions produce degraded experience.
- Not a substitute for full incident postmortems or for security incident handling (see security-and-compliance pages).

Key goals

1. Restore acceptable customer experience (meet SLOs or provide timely mitigation).
2. Maintain clear, time-boxed communications with customers and internal stakeholders.
3. Ensure predictable handoffs and escalation with minimal cognitive load for responders.

Incident severity classification (degradation-focused)

- Sev-2 (Degraded): Multiple customers report slow or flaky responses; error rate for a critical route > 2% for 5m; P99 latency > 2x target for 10m.
- Sev-3 (Minor Degradation): Single-customer impact or single-route increase in latency/error; transient and recoverable within 30 minutes.

SLO reference table

- API text-generation availability: 99.95% monthly.
- Per-route P99 latency target: 250ms for short-completion routes; alert at 500ms sustained over 10m.
- Embeddings throughput SLO: 95% of requests complete within 1s; alert at 1.5s sustained over 5m.

Ownership and roles

- Primary Responder (on-call engineer): Triage, initial mitigation, own incident until handoff.
- Secondary Responder: Assist with runbook steps and deeper debugging.
- Incident Commander (IC): Engages for Sev-2 or above; owns external communication cadence and escalation.
- Customer Success Liaison: Drafts customer-facing notes when customers are impacted.
- SRE Runbook Maintainer: Keeps runbook up to date; runs post-incident validation.

Response choreography (high level)

1. Detection: Alert or customer report. Primary responder acknowledges within 5 minutes.
2. Quick assessment (10 minutes): Determine scope (routes, regions, model variants, caching).
3. Immediate mitigation (time-boxed to first 30 minutes): Apply one of the standard mitigations below.
4. Escalation / IC: If not resolved after 30 minutes or if mitigation has customer-visible cost, escalate to IC.
5. Communication cadence: Status page + internal Slack thread within 15 minutes of acknowledging.
6. Post-incident: Postmortem within 72 hours, runbook updates in 1 week.

Standard mitigations (partial-degradation focus)

- Toggle degrade-to-compact-mode: Switch non-essential features to reduced model size or quantized variants. Example CLI:
  redwood-ops-cli service set-variant --service api-text --variant small-quant --reason "auto-degrade-latency"

- Route-level rate-limiting and quota bump: Reduce client-level burst windows temporarily.

- KV/prefix cache warm and rollback: If a KV cache miss storm is suspected, rehydrate popular prefixes from snapshot:
  aws s3 cp s3://redwood-cache-snapshots/prefix-hot-20260201 /tmp/prefixes && redwood-cache-load /tmp/prefixes

- Bypass expensive post-processing: Disable optional reranking or expensive decoding passes for affected routes.

- Model variant fallback: Route to a lower-latency variant in the same family. Ensure semantic compatibility.

Runbook: Partial-degradation — step-by-step (for Primary Responder)

1. Acknowledge alert and post initial note to #incident-redwood with incident summary template (see Communications templates).
2. Identify impacted routes and regions using:
   - Metrics: Grafana dashboard "API route health" (panel ids: api-route-errors, api-route-p99)
   - Traces: Jaeger service="api-gateway"
   - Logs: elasticsearch query: service:api AND level:error AND timestamp:>now-30m
3. Check model-serving pool health: redwood-ops-cli pool status --region us-west-2 --model-family gpt-xx
4. Attempt a low-risk mitigation (choose one):
   - Switch to fallback variant for affected route
   - Enable prefix cache from snapshot
   - Apply temporary circuit-breaker thresholds (example below)
5. Verify customer-visible metrics improve within 10 minutes. If not, escalate to IC.
6. Document all actions in incident tracker ticket and tag with labels: degradation, route:<route>, region:<region>.

Circuit-breaker thresholds (recommended starting points)

- If error-rate > 5% for 5m: trip circuit for non-critical endpoints (return 503 + Retry-After).
- If P99 latency > 1s for 10m: enable degraded-variant routing for read-only flows.

Handoff checklist (end of shift or escalation)

- Summary of what happened and current mitigation in place.
- Known diagnostics and next steps.
- Links to dashboards, logs, and active runbook commands.
- Escalation contacts and times (who to page next).

On-call rotation guidance and best practices

- 24/7 primary on-call per region with a 1:6 rotation. Secondary is scheduled for overlap during business hours.
- Weekly swap deadlines are Monday 09:00 UTC.
- The outgoing on-call must complete the handoff checklist in the incident ticket and post to #oncall-handoffs.
- Use the oncall-roster tool to update your availability: oncall-roster set-unavailable --from 2026-03-10 --to 2026-03-17 --reason "vacation"

Game day (simulation) plan focused on degradations

Purpose: Validate partial-degradation mitigation choreography and customer comm flow.
Frequency: Quarterly.
Participants: 1 IC, 2 primary responders, 1 customer success liaison, 1 observability engineer.
Runbook for game day

1. Inject synthetic load to a single route (tool: redwood-loadgen) to create P99 latency spike.
2. Confirm alerts fire and primary responder acknowledges within 5m.
3. Follow mitigation steps — prefer automated variant fallback first.
4. Customer Success drafts an initial status page and internal comm.
5. Simulate spinning new model pool from snapshot (test automation) and measure recovery time.
6. Debrief and update the runbook within 3 business days.

Incident postmortem template (use in conjunction with incident-comm-and-postmortem-framework)

- Title
- Incident ID / ticket
- Severity
- Timeline (UTC) — bullet list of time-stamped actions
- Root cause hypothesis and evidence
- Mitigations applied (what worked / didn’t work)
- Customer impact summary (routes impacted, customers and regions, duration)
- Action items (owner, deadline)
- Runbook updates required

Status page and customer communication templates

Initial public status (short form) — post within 15 minutes

- Title: Degraded performance for text-generation in US-West
- Status: Investigating
- Impact: Some requests may experience higher latency or transient errors. Customers using large-context generation may be most affected.
- Next update: 30 minutes

Customer-facing email / support template (initial)

Subject: Incident affecting text-generation latency — we're investigating

Hello <CustomerName>,

We are investigating an issue affecting text-generation latency in the US-West region. Some requests may take longer than usual or see transient errors. Our on-call team is actively working to restore normal performance and we will provide an update within 30 minutes.

If you have a mission-critical workload, reply to this message and we will prioritize mitigation for your traffic.

Sincerely,
Redwood Incident Response Team

Update template (follow-ups)

- T+30: What we have observed, mitigations attempted, and immediate next steps.
- T+60: If resolved, include recovery details and whether customers need to take any action. If unresolved, indicate escalation and expected timeline.

Resolution template (final)

- Title: Resolved — text-generation latency incident in US-West
- Status: Resolved
- Impact: <summary of affected routes, customers, total duration>
- Root cause: <concise cause statement>
- What we changed: <list of config/deployment changes>
- Postmortem: Link to detailed postmortem

Automation and tooling notes

- Use redwood-ops-cli for safe, auditable mitigations; every CLI action will create an audit entry.
- Integration with PagerDuty: Sev-2 pages escalate to SRE lead after 20 minutes without acknowledgment.
- Status page publishing is handled by status-publisher service: status-publisher post --component api-text --status investigating --message "Investigating elevated latency"

Maintenance and runbook ownership

- SRE Runbook Maintainer (rotating): updates runbooks after each postmortem.
- IC rotation: weekly; nominated IC details stored in the oncall-roster.

Appendix: Example incident Slack checklist (to paste into channel)

1. Incident title and ticket link
2. One-line impact summary
3. Primary responder name + pager link
4. Current mitigation (if any) and who applied it
5. Next steps and owner
6. T+30 update ETA

Appendix: Common diagnostics commands

- Check API route metrics: curl https://metrics-api.internal/query?panel=api-route-p99&from=-15m
- Pool status: redwood-ops-cli pool status --model-family gpt-xx
- Force variant fallback (dry-run): redwood-ops-cli route set-variant --route /v1/generate --variant small-quant --dry-run
